parallel.requirements: The parent and children recognized the required Node ESM .mjs deliverable, local-only imports, manual process.argv parsing, Base58 encode/decode parity, Python bytes repr formatting, and writing all code under /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated argparse and bytes/Base58 exploration while also implementing its own version; children were not isolated from the final /output tree, so ownership of the entry file and helpers overlapped.
parallel.implementation: The parent first created a flat helper layout with /output/test7.mjs and lib/*.mjs files, while children independently produced hierarchical modules and another /output/test7.mjs. The final tree used the hierarchical child-style modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent inspected the shared tree after noticing a race, removed duplicate flat helpers, and delivered a final artifact containing test7.mjs plus lib/base58, lib/cli, lib/text, and lib/runtime modules.
parallel.verification: The run compared samples and several CLI and byte-format probes against the executable, including missing args, help, repeated flags, negative-looking values, leading-zero decode, quote/backslash formatting, and invalid Base58.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 61 hidden cases. The trajectory does not expose the exact hidden mismatch, but it does expose cleanup and provenance churn from competing shared-workspace writes.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argv, no-dependency, Base58, bytes-format, and /output hierarchy requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery, with no subagents or cross-agent file ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote one consistent hierarchy: lib/base58/alphabet.mjs, lib/base58/codec.mjs, lib/cli/arg_parser.mjs, lib/format/python-bytes.mjs, lib/text/utf8.mjs, lib/index.mjs, and test7.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial agent composed the modules once, inventoried the final tree, and delivered the same entry-point name expected by the task without observed overwrite or cleanup churn.
serial.verification: The serial run verified the four samples and additional parser and byte-format cases including help abbreviations, explicit help values, empty strings, repeated flags, and expected-argument errors.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 61 hidden cases despite the coherent implementation and local checks; no concurrency-specific problem exists in the serial control.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the prompt constraints for pure Node ESM, .mjs suffixes, manual argv parsing, local-only imports, Base58, and Python bytes output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same prompt constraints and worked against the same executable behavior and samples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements-recognition difference is visible; both attempts aimed at the same behavior and both failed hidden tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned argparse and bytes/Base58 children while also implementing directly, creating overlapping ownership over final files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept probing, implementation, integration, and verification in one owner path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition created multiple implementation owners for the same output tree; serial had no delegation boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children returned useful findings and implementations, but no explicit file-ownership contract kept them from writing the same final entry and overlapping modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent did not transfer interface requirements across agents; module contracts were internal to one implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant interface difference was workspace/file ownership, not lost task context; parallel had cross-agent writes to shared final paths while serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implementation proceeded through a flat parent version and child hierarchical versions; the final code path was the child hierarchical tree adopted after inspection.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Implementation proceeded once through a single hierarchical module split with one apply_patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced similar functional areas, but the parallel path changed implementation provenance after competing writes, while serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received completed child reports and ultimately used a child-produced implementation, after some timeout waits and cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; the same agent progressed from probing to implementation to verification and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result handling included waiting for children and then selecting among returned/shared artifacts; serial had no result handoff lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple live actors wrote and deleted files in the same /output tree, including the required test7.mjs entry point and overlapping helpers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote one final tree and inventoried it without competing writes or cleanup from another actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel incurred a concrete deliverable overwrite and cleanup/adoption step; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent verified samples and selected edge cases after the final tree was settled, but official hidden coverage still failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent verified samples and several parser/bytes cases, including help-related and explicit-argument edge cases, but official hidden coverage also failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had substantial local verification yet insufficient official coverage; no verification difference explains an outcome gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and had several wait timeouts, but the parent still completed integration, cleanup, verification, and final delivery within the run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, took less agent time, and closed after direct verification and final inventory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more coordination effort and time, but not enough to establish budget exhaustion or a different official outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are identical: both parallel and serial failed with 80/141 tests. Therefore there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The meaningful difference is process-level: the parallel run suffered a concrete shared-output entry overwrite and cleanup/adoption churn, while the serial run built one coherent tree. The hidden evaluator failures are not attributable to that concurrency event from the available evidence.
parallel_contributors: Parallel had a realized deliverable overwrite and cleanup/adoption episode around /output/test7.mjs and helper modules.
Parallel still completed local verification and submitted a coherent hierarchical tree.
serial_contributors: Serial used a single-agent implementation path with no concurrent file ownership conflict.
Serial still failed the same official hidden-test count despite coherent local verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The final parallel tree used lib/base58/core.mjs and argparse_like.mjs, while serial used lib/base58/codec.mjs and arg_parser.mjs.
Both local verification suites were incomplete relative to the official hidden test set.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event only
